I let that sit for a second and said, "Okay. You just told your girlfriend that you're never going to marry her. Is that how you really feel, or is it just how you feel right now? So it's fine if you don't want to get married right now, and I don't expect that, but if you really, really don't ever want to get married again, we should talk about that."

He paused for a minute and said, "No. It's just how I feel right now." And we just continued our previous conversation.

He proposed about a year later, and we've been married for almost eighteen wonderful, happy years. We've talked about that discussion a couple of times, and each time he's said that while it was a little scary, he appreciated knowing where I stood and didn't take it as me pushing him into anything or as a sign that I expected a ring right away; he said/says I had a right to know and it was perfectly reasonable to say what I said.
